questions.q: What is the default trigger_rule for every task?
options: all_success — every upstream task must have succeeded
all_done — regardless of outcome
one_success — only one upstream task needs to succeed
There is no default; it must always be set explicitly
questions.explain: all_success is the default trigger rule, requiring every upstream task to have succeeded before the task runs.

questions.q: Which trigger rule fixes the 'join gets skipped after a branch' problem?
options: none_failed_min_one_success
all_failed
The default all_success works fine for this case
There is no trigger rule that fixes this
questions.explain: none_failed_min_one_success only requires that nothing failed and at least one upstream task succeeded — exactly matching a branch's expected shape.

questions.q: Which trigger rule is the natural choice for a cleanup or notification task that should run regardless of success or failure upstream?
options: all_done
all_success
one_failed
none_skipped
questions.explain: all_done runs the task once every upstream task has finished, regardless of whether they succeeded or failed.

questions.q: According to this lesson, when should you reach for a non-default trigger rule?
options: Only when the default all_success genuinely doesn't match what the task should do
On every single task, as a best practice
Never — the default should always be used
Only for tasks that use BashOperator
questions.explain: Changing the default without good reason can hide genuine failures instead of correctly propagating them — it should be a deliberate choice.

options: The condition controlling when a task runs, based on its upstream tasks' outcomes
How often a DAG is scheduled
Which worker a task runs on
